reviewStandard: Current identity and controlled identifiers were checked before generation against NCBI Taxonomy and current nomenclatural sources, with conservative morphology bounded by primary studies or referenced type-strain records. Candida auris and Candida glabrata were withheld because their routes used obsolete combinations; control subsequently retired those routes as audited aliases of uncovered candidozyma-auris and nakaseomyces-glabratus, and no raster was generated or rekeyed for either identity transition. Exactly one built-in generation call was made for each of the four supported subjects using the immutable passive prompt record. The WikiBiome media task and root inspected every copied PNG at original 1536 by 1024 resolution and reconciled visible bodies and groupings without trusting prompt counts. Root accepted the four exact drafts, and only those files were promoted after approved review-log records and all release gates were established.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI Taxonomy records Candida tropicalis as the current species NCBITaxon:5482. Primary microscopy supports spherical-to-ovoid budding bodies and pseudohyphal or hyphal forms. This selected plate uses only oval blastoconidia, one bud pair, and one short pseudohyphal chain; it makes no diagnostic or colony-color claim.
assets.visualReview: Exactly eight cellular bodies appear in five separated groupings: three isolated oval singles across the upper field, one lower-left touching mother-and-bud pair, and one lower-right linear three-body pseudohyphal chain with two pinched junctions. No branching network, colony plate, host material, labels, scale bar, scenery, edge clipping, or watermark is visible.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI Taxonomy and LPSN recognize Caulobacter as current genus NCBITaxon:75. The plate is a static selection, not a lifecycle scene or genus-diagnostic claim.

Two rods—upper right and lower left—each have one short narrow straight polar stalk with a blunt end; five rods have no external structure.
